title: Beyond the Time Constant: Output–Persistence Dissociation in Human Post-Rotatory Eye-Movement Responses
abstract: Classical velocity-storage models describe post-rotatory eye velocity as the observable output of direct and stored vestibular components, yet rotational testing is often summarized primarily by the decay time constant. We examined whether the magnitudes of directional output asymmetry and decay-persistence asymmetry covary. This single-center registry-based observational analysis used source-reconciled data from 40 fast-domain-eligible patients; 31 had complete bilateral post-rotatory slow-phase velocity (SPV) and time-constant (TC) measurements. SPV-AR and TC-AR were calculated as normalized absolute inter-directional differences, thus retaining asymmetry magnitude but not its sign. In the 31 complete datasets (16 women, 15 men; median age 56 years, IQR 40.5–61.5; range 19–78), the median SPV-AR was 26.9% (IQR 12.5–37.0) and the median TC-AR was 34.8% (IQR 12.7–59.6). The magnitudes of SPV-AR and TC-AR were not detectably associated (Spearman ρ = 0.091, p = 0.626; Pearson r = 0.031, p = 0.868). Mean post-rotatory SPV and mean TC also showed no statistically significant association. Output magnitude and temporal persistence provide complementary, non-interchangeable descriptors of the measured ocular response; this analysis does not establish directional sign concordance, physiological independence, or diagnostic thresholds.
